item.title: Colleagues praise boat captain's courage after six health workers rescued from sea ordeal

item.content:encoded:
Boat captain Risiate Senilagakali, who helped save six health workers after they went missing at sea in Lau for more than 30 hours, has been praised by his colleagues for his courage and dedication, with one describing their relief at seeing him safe after the ordeal.

Senilagakali had earlier tried to swim towards Aiwa Island and was rescued on Thursday morning, while the six Ministry of Health workers were rescued on Thursday night after they spent more than 30 hours drifting at sea when their boat encountered engine problems.

Speaking after visiting Senilagakali, Eastern Health Division General Services staff member Temo Colavanua says they were overjoyed to see him safe.

Colavanua says when they first heard the group had gone missing, they could understand what they were going through because they had experienced similar sea journeys themselves.

He says they were deeply worried, but never lost hope, as their faith kept them strong throughout the ordeal.

Colavanua says they know Senilagakali well and have always admired his commitment and dedication to his work.

He says seeing Senilagakali safe has brought great joy and relief to everyone.

Meanwhile, the Ministry of Health praised Senilagakali describing him as a hero, claiming he swam through rough seas to alert authorities, helping to save the lives of the six health workers.

They say his courage inspired hope across the country as people prayed for the safe return of the group.

The six health workers are now receiving medical treatment at Twomey Hospital in Tamavua after being flown from Lakeba to Suva on Friday.

item.title: Human Rights Commission calls for zero tolerance on torture after alleged inmate assault
item.description: The Fiji Human Rights and Anti-Discrimination Commission is calling for zero tolerance on torture and all forms of ill-treatment following a viral video showing the alleged assault of an inmate by a Fiji Corrections Service officer at the Lautoka Remand Centre. The Commission welcomes the Fiji Corrections Service's decision to launch a formal investigation into the incident.
item.content:encoded:
The Fiji Human Rights and Anti-Discrimination Commission is calling for zero tolerance on torture and all forms of ill-treatment following a viral video showing the alleged assault of an inmate by a Fiji Corrections Service officer at the Lautoka Remand Centre.

The Commission welcomes the Fiji Corrections Service's decision to launch a formal investigation into the incident.

Director Loukinikini Lewaravu says the inmate should receive immediate medical attention, appropriate care and any necessary support while the investigation is underway.

Lewaravu says every person, including those in detention, has the right to be treated with dignity and humanity, and people deprived of their liberty remain entitled to the full protection of their human rights.

She says the investigation should be conducted promptly, independently, impartially and transparently.

Lewaravu says if the allegations are proven, those responsible must be held accountable in accordance with the law.

She adds the Commission will continue to monitor the matter and has reaffirmed the importance of upholding human rights in all places of detention.

item.title: PM Rabuka meets Health Workers after dramatic sea rescue
item.description: Navitalai Naivalurua · 02/08/2026 Prime Minister Sitiveni Rabuka took time this afternoon to visit the six health professionals who were lost at sea in Lau for more than 30 hours.
item.content:encoded:
Navitalai Naivalurua · 02/08/2026

Prime Minister Sitiveni Rabuka took time this afternoon to visit the six health professionals who were lost at sea in Lau for more than 30 hours.

The six are receiving medical treatment at Twomey Hospital in Tamavua after being flown from Lakeba to Suva on Friday.

According to the Ministry of Health, the team departed Moce Island at 7am on Wednesday bound for Oneata and was expected to arrive about two hours later.

After they failed to arrive as scheduled, the district nurse in Oneata contacted the Lakeba Sub-Divisional Hospital, prompting search and rescue efforts.

The Ministry says the boat handler was found on Thursday morning and told rescuers that after the engine failed, the vessel began taking on water.

The medical team removed the wooden floorboards from the boat to use as flotation devices while wearing their life jackets.

In an effort to get mobile phone reception, the boat handler swam towards Aiwa Island, leaving the rest of the medical team together and safe in the water.

The six healthcare workers were eventually rescued on Thursday night by the captain and crew of Lomaiviti Princess 12.
